profound-rf.summary: Clinic radiofrequency microneedling system that firms sagging skin and softens wrinkles and acne scars by rebuilding collagen at depth.

quick.overview:
Profound is a radiofrequency (RF) microneedling system used in aesthetic clinics. People turn to it for firmer skin, softer wrinkles and smoother acne scars, which are the changes it is aimed at.

Fine needles enter the skin and deliver RF energy at depth, which prompts a healing response and collagen remodeling over the following weeks. Research on the device is mostly registered device studies, including cellulite, wrinkle and acne-scar studies and a 500-person feasibility study of the Profound Matrix system.
quick.how: It is performed in a clinic by a trained provider, usually as a short in-office session with numbing applied first. Results build gradually as collagen remodels, and people often combine it with other skin treatments or a sunscreen routine.
quick.risks: Redness and swelling after microneedling are expected for a few days. Infection is a concern when the procedure is done in unregulated settings with poor infection control. Device-specific safety findings are not summarized in the available sources.

angle.text: Profound is used for firmer skin, softer wrinkles and smoother acne scars. Needles deliver radiofrequency energy at depth, which triggers collagen remodeling over the following weeks. It is documented mainly in registered device studies.

secret-rf.summary: Cutera's fractional microneedle RF device used in clinics to improve skin quality and soften facial wrinkles.

quick.overview:
Secret RF is a fractional radiofrequency microneedling device from Cutera, used in clinics for better skin quality and fewer facial wrinkles.

Fine needles enter the skin and deliver RF energy in a fractional pattern, which stimulates collagen remodeling as the skin heals. Two trials were registered in 2018; results are not summarized in the available sources.
quick.how: Treatment is done in a clinic by a trained provider. Results develop gradually over weeks as the skin remodels, and people commonly add a series of sessions or pair it with a standard skincare routine.
quick.risks: Expected effects are redness and swelling for a few days. Infection is a general microneedling risk when infection control is poor. Device-specific safety data are not covered in the available sources.

angle.text: Secret RF is used for better skin quality and fewer facial wrinkles. Microneedles deliver radiofrequency energy in a fractional pattern, which prompts collagen remodeling as the skin heals. Two registered studies exist.

vivace-rf-microneedling.summary: RF microneedling device offered in aesthetic clinics for tighter, smoother-looking skin.

quick.overview:
Vivace is an RF microneedling device offered in aesthetic clinics, used by people who want tighter, smoother skin and better texture.

Like others in the category, it pairs needle punctures with radiofrequency energy to prompt collagen remodeling. No study located names the Vivace device itself; a registered 2023 trial examined fractional microneedling RF as a category for facial aging.
quick.how: It is performed in a clinic by a trained provider in a short session, typically repeated in a series. Skin tightening and texture changes appear gradually as the skin heals and remodels.
quick.risks: Redness and swelling are expected for a few days after treatment. Infection is a general microneedling concern when procedures are done without proper infection control. Device-specific risks are not documented in the available sources.

angle.text: Vivace is used for tighter, smoother skin and better texture. Needle punctures plus radiofrequency energy prompt collagen remodeling as the skin heals. No study located names the Vivace device itself; a trial has looked at the wider category.

potenza-rf.summary: Cynosure's RF microneedling system used to smooth wrinkles, scars, stretch marks and pigmentation and improve skin quality.

quick.overview:
Potenza is a clinic-based RF microneedling system from Cynosure. People use it for smoother skin with fewer wrinkles, fine lines, scars, stretch marks and pigmentation.

Needles enter the skin and deliver radiofrequency energy, which stimulates collagen remodeling during healing. Available documentation is a handful of registered device studies with 8 to 79 participants.
quick.how: Treatment is performed by a clinician, usually as a series of sessions spaced weeks apart. Changes in texture and tone build gradually as the skin remodels.
quick.risks: Redness and swelling are expected for a few days. Infection is a general microneedling concern in unregulated settings. Device-specific safety findings are not summarized in the available sources.

angle.text: Potenza is used to smooth wrinkles, fine lines, scars, stretch marks and pigmentation. RF microneedling prompts collagen remodeling as the skin heals. Evidence comes mainly from small registered studies.

sofwave.summary: Needle-free ultrasound skin-lifting system used to lift the brow, neck and under-chin and soften fine lines with minimal downtime.

quick.overview:
Sofwave is a needle-free ultrasound system used to lift the brow, neck and under-chin and to soften fine lines, with minimal downtime. A 2023 review lists it as FDA-cleared.

Ultrasound energy heats the dermis and subdermal tissue, causing controlled thermal injury that leads to collagen remodeling and lifting. The review describes clinically significant results for eyebrow, submental and neck lift and fine-line reduction, and Sofwave has been registered in many studies for laxity, wrinkles, acne scars and cellulite.
quick.how: It is done in a clinic by a trained provider in a single short session, with no needles and little recovery. Lifting develops over the following weeks to months as collagen remodels.
quick.risks: Side effects are not detailed in the available sources. The 2023 review stresses careful patient selection and managing expectations about the size of the result.

angle.text: Sofwave is used to lift the brow, neck and under-chin and soften fine lines with minimal downtime. Ultrasound heats the dermis without needles, prompting collagen remodeling. A 2023 review describes clinically significant lift results across many registered trials.

ultherapy-prime.summary: Updated Ultherapy ultrasound device with better imaging that lifts and tightens the lower face, neck and brow without surgery.

quick.overview:
Ultherapy Prime is the newer version of the Ultherapy skin-lifting device. Clinics use it for non-surgical lifting of the brow, lower face, under-chin and neck, and tightening of the decolletage.

Focused ultrasound, guided by live imaging, heats tiny points at chosen depths in the deep dermis and fascia. This is reported to stimulate new collagen and elastin and a tightening effect. Published data on the Prime model are so far early case series, a survey and a preprint; the wider MFU-V category is FDA-cleared for brow lifting, neck and submental tightening and decolletage wrinkles.
quick.how: A clinician performs it in a single office session, using the imaging screen to place energy at the right depths. Tightening develops gradually over the following months. People interested in jawline and neck definition often use it as a non-surgical option.
quick.risks: A 2025 survey compared patient-reported pain, redness and swelling between Prime and the older system. Treatment is performed by clinicians.

angle.text: Ultherapy Prime is used for non-surgical lifting of the lower face, jawline and neck. Focused ultrasound with live imaging heats deep tissue, prompting new collagen and tightening. Data on the Prime model are early; the original Ultherapy has a broader record.

ulthera-deepsee.summary: Ulthera's imaging-guided ultrasound system that tightens the lower face and under-chin for a sharper jawline without surgery.

quick.overview:
DeepSEE is an Ulthera ultrasound system with built-in imaging, used by clinicians to tighten lax skin on the lower face and under the chin for a firmer jawline.

Microfocused ultrasound delivers heat at set depths below the skin surface, while imaging lets the operator see tissue layers and target them. A single-arm study of 201 participants for lower-face and submental laxity was registered and completed; its results were not available in the sources reviewed.
quick.how: It is performed by a trained clinician in an office session. Tightening builds over the following weeks to months, and it is used by people who want a non-surgical option for lower-face laxity.
quick.risks: Specific adverse-event data for this model were not available in the reviewed sources. MFU-V devices are discussed in the literature as noninvasive alternatives to surgery.

angle.text: DeepSEE is used for non-surgical tightening of the lower face and under-chin, aiming at a sharper jawline. Imaging-guided focused ultrasound heats tissue at set depths so the operator can target it. A 201-person study is registered.

doublo-hifu.summary: Korean HIFU device used to tighten facial and neck skin with focused ultrasound; two small studies in Asian patients exist.

quick.overview:
Doublo is a Korean-made intense focused ultrasound (HIFU) device used to tighten facial and neck skin without surgery.

Focused ultrasound heats tissue at various depths below the surface while sparing the surface layer, prompting collagen remodeling and tightening. Two small studies in Asian patients have been published: a 2015 study of 11 patients on histologic change, safety and efficacy, and a 2020 study of 43 patients on neck and lower-face laxity whose authors described good safety but limited efficacy.
quick.how: It is used in clinics by trained providers as an in-office session aimed at mild-to-moderate laxity of the lower face and neck. Changes, where they occur, develop gradually over weeks to months.
quick.risks: The 2020 study describes IFUS as having a good safety profile. Details beyond that were not available in the reviewed sources.

angle.text: Doublo is a Korean HIFU device used for facial and neck skin tightening. Focused ultrasound heats deep tissue and prompts collagen remodeling. Two small published studies in Asian patients have examined it, one reporting limited efficacy.

ultraformer-iii.summary: Korean HIFU lifting device used in clinics for non-surgical facial lifting and a more defined lower face.

quick.overview:
Ultraformer III is a Korean HIFU machine used in clinics for non-surgical facial lifting and skin rejuvenation, with a more defined lower face as the goal.

Focused ultrasound heats tissue at selected depths, which is described as promoting collagen synthesis and reducing subcutaneous fat. Published studies are small cohorts, mostly on the related Ultraformer MPT, looking at lifting by facial area with 3D scanning, eyelid sagging and ultrasound frequency.
quick.how: A clinician performs it in an office session, treating the lower face, jawline and neck. Lifting appears gradually over weeks to months as collagen remodels.
quick.risks: Safety details are limited to the studies' own safety evaluations. Several larger device trials are registered.

angle.text: Ultraformer III is used for facial lifting and a more defined lower face. HIFU heats deep tissue, promoting collagen and tightening. Published studies are small and mostly cover the related Ultraformer MPT model.

thermage-flx.summary: In-office monopolar radiofrequency device that tightens lax skin and softens wrinkles on the face, eye area and body without surgery.

quick.overview:
Thermage FLX is a clinic-based machine that uses monopolar radiofrequency energy to tighten lax skin and soften wrinkles on the face, eye area, neck and body without surgery. The Thermage line was the first monopolar RF skin-tightening system FDA-cleared, for the eye area in 2002.

RF current is converted to heat by tissue resistance, warming the dermis while surface cooling protects the skin. The heat is said to contract existing collagen right away and trigger new collagen over weeks to months. Research is largely small studies, practitioner surveys and device-company-linked trials, with reports of gradual, modest improvement over months.
quick.how: Trained clinicians deliver it in a single office session. Results build over several months and are described as lasting about one to two years. In forums it is discussed as a non-surgical option for jawline and facial laxity.
quick.risks: Reported effects include redness, swelling and pain, with burns, blistering, pigment change, dents, scarring and fat loss described less commonly. Pacemakers and pregnancy are listed contraindications.

angle.text: Thermage FLX is used to tighten the face, eye area and body and soften wrinkles without surgery. Radiofrequency heats the deep skin, contracting collagen and prompting new collagen over months. The evidence is many small studies and few controlled trials.

exilis-ultra-exilis-elite.summary: BTL's radiofrequency platform for non-surgical skin tightening and body contouring on the face and body.

quick.overview:
Exilis is a BTL radiofrequency machine used in clinics for non-surgical skin tightening and body contouring on the face and body. Ultra and Elite are newer versions of the platform. Wikipedia lists it among commercial RF skin-tightening devices.

RF current is converted to heat in the skin, with the aim of contracting collagen and prompting new collagen over months, tightening lax skin and fine lines. RF devices are described as an alternative to facelifts and other surgery, used on jowls, abdomen, thighs and arms. The sources reviewed describe the RF category in general; model-specific trial data were not found.
quick.how: Clinicians deliver it in a series of in-office sessions with little downtime. Results build over months.
quick.risks: Category reports include redness, swelling, pain, burns, blistering, pigment change and, less commonly, scarring or fat loss. Pacemakers and pregnancy are listed contraindications.

angle.text: Exilis is used for non-surgical tightening of the face and body. Radiofrequency heats the skin, contracting collagen and prompting new collagen over months. Sources reviewed describe the RF category more than this device specifically.

venus-legacy.summary: Venus Concept's RF plus pulsed-magnetic-field device for tightening skin and smoothing contours on the face and body.

quick.overview:
Venus Legacy is a clinic-based device from Venus Concept that combines multipolar radiofrequency, pulsed electromagnetic fields and suction. It is used for skin laxity, wrinkles, cellulite and mild fat reduction for smoother, firmer contours on the face and body.

Radiofrequency heats tissue to prompt collagen remodeling, and the pulsed fields and suction are added by the manufacturer's design. The published evidence found is a 2015 overview article presenting it among newer RF devices, and a couple of small registered studies.
quick.how: It is delivered by clinicians in a series of in-office sessions with little downtime. Changes in firmness and contour build gradually over weeks to months.
quick.risks: Reported RF effects include redness, swelling, pain, burns and pigment change, and rarely scarring or fat loss. Pacemakers and pregnancy are listed contraindications.

angle.text: Venus Legacy is used for skin laxity, wrinkles, cellulite and mild fat reduction on the face and body. RF heat plus magnetic fields and suction tighten skin and smooth contours. Published evidence is a short review and small registered studies.

venus-viva.summary: Nanofractional RF resurfacing device used for smoother skin, softer acne scars and fewer wrinkles with shorter recovery than ablative options.

quick.overview:
Venus Viva is a clinic device that delivers radiofrequency energy through tiny pins to resurface skin. People use it for smoother texture, softer acne scars and fewer wrinkles.

Fractional RF heats microscopic zones of skin through micro-pins, leaving surrounding tissue intact, which is described as shortening recovery compared with surgery or full ablation. Published work is mainly small studies, including a 20-patient acne-scar study in Indian skin (Fitzpatrick types IV-V) and a retrospective patient-satisfaction study.
quick.how: It is performed by clinicians in a series of sessions. Skin texture and scars improve gradually as the skin remodels over the weeks after treatment.
quick.risks: Fractional resurfacing generally causes redness and swelling for a period after treatment; burns and pigment change are reported RF risks. Little device-specific safety data appear in the sources reviewed.

angle.text: Venus Viva is used for smoother skin, softer acne scars and fewer wrinkles with shorter recovery than ablative approaches. Nanofractional RF micro-pins resurface the skin. Support comes from small uncontrolled studies.

pelleve.summary: Ellman's 4-MHz monopolar RF system for softening wrinkles and mildly tightening skin on the face, neck and hands.

quick.overview:
Pellevé is a clinic-based monopolar radiofrequency system from Ellman International, used to soften wrinkles and mildly firm skin on the face and neck and, in one study, the hands. It was one of the RF devices that followed Thermage after 2002.

Continuous 4-MHz radiofrequency energy heats the skin to a therapeutic temperature, with the aim of contracting collagen and stimulating new collagen. Published work includes a 17-patient facial study, a 31-patient hand-wrinkle study and a 12-patient periorbital cohort.
quick.how: A clinician delivers it in an office session, often repeated in a short series. Visible tightening develops as collagen remodels over the following weeks.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed give little safety detail. Category-wide RF reports include pain, burns, pigment change and rare scarring or fat loss.

angle.text: Pellevé is used to soften wrinkles and mildly tighten skin on the face and neck. Monopolar 4-MHz radiofrequency heats the skin, contracting collagen and prompting new collagen. Evidence comes from small uncontrolled studies of 12 to 31 patients.

bodytite.summary: InMode's radiofrequency-assisted liposuction that removes fat and tightens the overlying skin for a leaner, tighter body contour.

quick.overview:
BodyTite is a radiofrequency-assisted liposuction system from InMode. It removes fat and heats the tissue so the skin tightens, aiming at a leaner contour with less loose skin than liposuction alone. It is used on the abdomen, flanks, arms and thighs.

A probe under the skin delivers bipolar RF energy that liquefies fat and heats surrounding tissue with temperature monitoring, and the fat is then aspirated. Published reports describe it as filling a gap between liposuction and excisional surgery such as brachioplasty or abdominoplasty. Evidence is mostly surgeon-authored series and retrospective reviews, plus small registered studies.
quick.how: It is a surgical procedure performed by a surgeon, typically under local or general anesthesia, followed by a recovery period with compression and swelling that settles over weeks. Final contour is judged once swelling resolves.
quick.risks: Reported effects include swelling, bruising and numbness, with burns, infection, seroma, hematoma and asymmetry described as less common. A 97-patient series reported major complications in 6.25% of patients per one summary. US FDA clearance covers electrocoagulation and hemostasis rather than body contouring as such.

angle.text: BodyTite removes fat while tightening the overlying skin, for a leaner contour with less loose skin than liposuction alone. RF energy liquefies fat before it is aspirated and heats the skin so it contracts. The contour change is the result of the procedure; evidence is mostly surgeon-reported series.

accutite.summary: InMode's small-area radiofrequency-assisted lipolysis tool that trims jowl and neck fat and tightens skin for a more defined lower face.

quick.overview:
AccuTite is a minimally invasive radiofrequency device from InMode that heats tissue under the skin to tighten it and reduce small fat deposits, mainly on the jowls and neck, for a more defined lower face.

RF energy is delivered into the subdermal space to heat dermal collagen and fat, targeting skin laxity and excess fat together. Surgeons present it as an option for people whose laxity is too much for noninvasive devices but who do not want or need a facelift, with less downtime and cost than open procedures like neck lifts. Evidence is small registered studies, case series and reviews.
quick.how: It is performed by a clinician through small entry points, usually under local anesthesia. Swelling settles over weeks, and the tightened contour is assessed once it resolves.
quick.risks: Reviews describe lower risk than revision facelifts, but no detailed complication rates for AccuTite appear in the literature reviewed, and the studies are small.

angle.text: AccuTite is used on the jowls and neck to reduce small fat deposits and tighten skin, for a more defined lower face with less downtime than a neck lift. RF heat under the skin melts fat and tightens tissue. Evidence is small studies and surgeon reviews.

vaser-liposuction.summary: Ultrasound-assisted liposuction used for body contouring and abs etching, removing fat around muscle to show more definition.

quick.overview:
VASER is a brand of ultrasound-assisted liposuction. It is widely associated with high-definition liposculpture, sometimes called abdominal etching, where fat is removed or shaped to show the outline of muscles such as the abdominals.

A probe delivers ultrasonic energy into the fat layer to loosen it before it is suctioned out. Surgeons who developed the approach describe treating superficial fat layers to define musculature as well as reduce volume. Published work is largely surgeon-reported case series, with a few small comparative trials against conventional suction liposuction. Liposuction removes fat locally and does not produce lasting weight loss.
quick.how: It is a surgical procedure done by a surgeon under anesthesia, followed by compression garments and a recovery period while swelling settles. Definition becomes visible once the area has healed.
quick.risks: Liposuction in general carries reported risks including infection, bleeding, blood clots, organ perforation and fat embolism, with risk rising with the volume removed. A dedicated review covers complications of high-definition liposculpture.

angle.text: VASER is used for body contouring and abs etching, where fat removal around muscle shows more definition. Ultrasound loosens fat before it is suctioned out. The change is visible once healed; evidence is mostly surgeon case series and a few small trials.

power-assisted-liposuction-pal.summary: Motorized, vibrating-cannula liposuction used to remove stubborn fat for a leaner, smoother body contour.

quick.overview:
Power-assisted liposuction uses a cannula driven by a motor so it vibrates as it moves through fat. People use it to remove stubborn fat for a leaner, smoother contour, and it is also described for male chest reduction and fat harvesting.

The motorized handpiece moves the cannula rapidly back and forth, which proponents say lowers the surgeon's effort and eases passage through fat. It is typically paired with tumescent anesthetic solution. Published work is mostly surgeons describing their technique, and few randomized trials compare it with conventional liposuction.
quick.how: It is a surgical operation performed by a surgeon, followed by compression garments and several weeks of swelling that settles. The final contour shows after healing.
quick.risks: It shares liposuction risks reported in the literature, including pain, bruising, contour irregularities, infection, bleeding and clots, with rare deaths. Risk is reported to increase with the volume removed.

angle.text: PAL is a motorized liposuction variant used to remove stubborn fat in a smooth, controlled way. A vibrating cannula takes out local fat deposits for a leaner contour once healed. Few trials compare it directly with conventional liposuction.

water-assisted-liposuction-bodyjet.summary: Liposuction using a pressurized fan-shaped water jet to loosen fat for body contouring and fat transfer.

quick.overview:
Water-assisted liposuction uses a jet of fluid to loosen fat while it is suctioned out, for a leaner body contour. BodyJet is a branded system. It is also used to collect fat for transfer to other areas such as the breast.

A fan-shaped water jet through the cannula delivers fluid and anesthetic and detaches fat, which is then aspirated. Published research is concentrated in fat-grafting and tissue-quality studies, such as case series and lab comparisons, rather than in contouring outcomes.
quick.how: It is a surgical procedure done by a surgeon, usually with compression garments afterwards and a recovery of several weeks. The contour change shows once swelling settles.
quick.risks: Risks are those of liposuction generally, including pain, bruising, contour irregularity, infection, bleeding, clots and rare deaths. No device-specific safety data were identified.

angle.text: Water-assisted liposuction, including the BodyJet system, is used for fat removal and body contouring. A water jet loosens fat before it is aspirated, and the leaner contour shows after healing. Research is mainly on fat harvesting.

tumescent-liposuction.summary: The standard liposuction technique, done under local anesthesia with dilute lidocaine, for slimmer, more defined contours.

quick.overview:
Tumescent liposuction fills fat with a dilute numbing solution before suction, so the patient can stay awake under local anesthesia. It is used on areas such as the abdomen, flanks, neck and jowls for a slimmer, more defined contour, and also for lipedema.

Lidocaine numbs the tissue and epinephrine narrows blood vessels, reducing bleeding and bruising while fat is aspirated through thin cannulas. It was developed by dermatologist Jeffrey Klein in the 1980s and is now a standard technique. Large surveys of dermatologic surgeons have examined its safety, and studies report good long-term results in lipedema.
quick.how: A surgeon performs it in a procedure room, usually with local anesthesia only. Compression garments are worn afterwards, and the contour shows once swelling settles over weeks.
quick.risks: The literature reports lidocaine toxicity as the technique-specific concern, plus general liposuction risks such as infection, bleeding, clots and contour irregularity. A 1999 report noted deaths and that reporting is not mandatory, so incidence is uncertain.

angle.text: Tumescent liposuction removes localized fat under local anesthesia, used on the abdomen, flanks, neck and jowls for a slimmer, more defined contour. Dilute lidocaine numbs and swells the fat before it is suctioned out. The change is visible after healing; safety data come from large surgeon surveys.
